title: Reproducing the Hidden-Objective Audit on a Tiny Open Model Organism

original_idea.body: Apply cheap interpretability (SAE inspection or linear probing) to a public backdoor/sleeper-agent open model to blind-detect a hidden trigger/objective; report detection success and FPR.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: showing whether cheap lab-free interpretability catches a planted hidden objective targets a recognized top medium-horizon threat (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Blind auditing for an unknown trigger requires real interpretability judgment and a suitable model organism; intermediate (level 3).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable but depends on a suitable open model organism and open-ended auditing (level 4).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Hidden-objective model-organism auditing on public checkpoints is neglected, high-counterfactual work (level 5).

low_compute.reasoning: Small open model + SAE/probing inference; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: A minimal reproducible open version described as missing; mostly novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Minimal open reproducible hidden-objective audit appears mostly novel.
